title: dev-code-review review.json — machine review verdict (incl. R3 masking judge)
description: The ratified output of the dev-code-review skill, written to <evid_root>/<key>/review.json. The recipe branches on `verdict` (approve advances, request-changes routes back to dev-fix); `masking` carries the R3 symptom-masking judge's call. Ratified against samples/EXAMPLE-defect-loop/review.json. v1.3.0 (additive, backward compatible): findings may carry an integer `line`, the new-file line of the added or changed line; the reviewer eval scorer (dev-code-review/scripts/reviewer_eval.py) locates a catch by file + line. v1.4.0 (additive, backward compatible): findings may carry `bug_class`, the CLASS of the bug from a closed vocabulary, and `instances`, the other places in the same diff where that class occurs, so one finding covers the class and every instance gets fixed; file + bug_class is the fingerprint review_rounds.py records and recipe_router.py --review-rounds uses to detect a finding that survives fix cycles (stagnation). v1.5.0 (additive, backward compatible): optional `headline`, the count lead `review_brief.py finalize` writes (summary starts with it; a clean review reads exactly `0 findings: nothing needs fixing.`), and optional `brief`, the record of the per-area reviewer brief (conventions `review_brief`): which changed files were skipped, which skips were refused because the file is R6-denylisted or shared core, and how many low findings the nit cap withheld; findings[].withheld / withheld_reason are now documented. validate.py DEV-REVIEW-H1 (the headline count equals the open findings and leads the summary) and DEV-REVIEW-B1 (open lows within brief.max_nits; no file both skipped and refused; an unavailable brief skips and withholds nothing) fire only when those fields are present. v1.6.0 (additive, backward compatible): optional `validation`, the record of independent finding validation written by dev-code-review/scripts/finding_votes.py tally (never by hand): `validators` fresh Agent validators voted on every candidate finding and a finding is reported only with at least `quorum` confirms at or above `confidence_floor` (loop-limits review_validation); findings[].finding_id and findings[].votes are now documented. validate.py DEV-REVIEW-V1 (every open finding carries votes.confirm >= quorum, the open findings number `kept`, the counts add up) fires only when `validation` is present.

verdict.description: The machine verdict the recipe acts on. Masking suspected => request-changes.

masking.description: The R3 masking judge's call: true = the diff greens the test by hiding the symptom (swallowed exception, suppressed log, narrow special-case).

findings.description: Validated findings only: validated by independent validators at quorum (v1.6.0); the floor and quorum are loop-limits review_validation. Earlier findings carried with resolved: true need no votes. May be empty on a clean approve.

dimension.description: Which specialist raised it (security, performance, framework_patterns, test_coverage, accessibility, architecture, masking).

file.description: The file the finding is about: repo-relative path, forward slashes, no leading ./

line.description: OPTIONAL (v1.3.0). The NEW-file line number of the added or changed line the finding is about (the same line the validator re-reads at file:line). An integer, never a range or a string: reviewer_eval.py matches a finding to a confirmed bug by file + line, and a finding with no integer line is unlocatable and cannot count as a catch.

finding_id.description: OPTIONAL (documented v1.6.0). The candidate id finding_votes.py ballot assigns: `F-` + the first 10 hex of sha1(dimension|file|line|bug_class|normalized issue). The key the validators vote on.

votes.description: OPTIONAL (documented v1.6.0). The independent validators' tally for this finding, written by finding_votes.py tally. confirm counts confirms at or above validation.confidence_floor; reject and pre_existing count those verdicts at any confidence; cast is the number of returned ballots. DEV-REVIEW-V1: an open finding needs confirm >= validation.quorum and cast == validation.validators_returned.

bug_class.description: OPTIONAL (v1.4.0). The CLASS of the bug, not its instance. A CLOSED vocabulary on purpose: two blind reviewers in different rounds must pick the same word for the fingerprint to be stable. file + bug_class is the stagnation fingerprint (review_rounds.py); `other` (or no class) falls back to a weaker fingerprint on the normalised issue text, which rewording defeats. One line per class: dev-code-review/references/specialists.md.

instances.description: OPTIONAL (v1.4.0). The OTHER places in this diff where the same bug_class occurs, so one finding covers the class and the fixer fixes every instance, not only the anchored line. The anchored file/line is not repeated here.

withheld.description: OPTIONAL (documented v1.5.0). true = kept in review.json for the human but not posted and not counted as open: dev-pr-feed's per-PR volume cap, or review_brief.py finalize's nit cap. review_rounds.py and validate.py DEV-REVIEW-H1 exclude it from the open findings.

withheld_reason.description: OPTIONAL (documented v1.5.0). Why it was withheld, e.g. `volume cap (max_threads_per_pr=N): ...` or `nit cap (review_brief max_nits=N): ...`.

harden.description: OPTIONAL (v1.2.0). Set when the reviewer judges this is a mistake a check could catch, so it should not be corrected by hand again. The reviewer only DRAFTS: it never writes a rule, a queue line or the conventions file. dev-harden collects these blocks between runs, groups them by candidate_rule.id across tickets, proves the rule with rule_probe.py and proposes it; a human applies it; dev-pre-pr enforces it from then on.

band.description: The highest fix-ladder band the reviewer believes can catch it.

why.description: The recurring mistake and the right move, in one sentence.

candidate_rule.description: band=static only: a draft conventions rule (dev-pre-pr/references/violation-rules.md). Its `fix` is written TO the next agent: what to do instead and where the real fix lives.

must_trip.description: A line the draft rule must flag, usually the offending line from this diff.

must_pass.description: The compliant version the rule must NOT flag.

summary.description: The reviewer's overall rationale — why this verdict.

headline.description: OPTIONAL (v1.5.0). The count lead, written by dev-code-review/scripts/review_brief.py finalize from the OPEN findings (not resolved, not withheld): `0 findings: nothing needs fixing.` or `N finding(s) (<c> critical, <h> high, <m> medium, <l> low).` with only non-zero severities. `summary` starts with it and so does the first line of review.md. DEV-REVIEW-H1 checks the count.

brief.description: OPTIONAL (v1.5.0). The per-area reviewer brief (conventions `review_brief`) as review_brief.py finalize applied it. Absent = the conventions file has no brief (today's behaviour). `unavailable` = a brief exists but could not be applied honestly (malformed, the R6 scan could not run, no decided nit cap, or the diff changes the conventions file): everything was reviewed and nothing withheld.

max_nits.description: The nit cap applied: the brief's own max_nits, else loop-limits review_brief.default_max_nits.

nits_withheld.description: Low findings stamped withheld by the nit cap.

skipped.description: Changed files matched by a skip_paths glob and not handed to the specialists.

skip_refused.description: Changed files a skip_paths glob matched that the brief may never skip: hit by the R6 denylist (the adopter list or the framework floor) or by shared_core_globs. Reviewed as normal.

areas.description: The brief areas whose path_globs matched a changed file.

validation.description: OPTIONAL (v1.6.0). How the candidate findings were validated, written by dev-code-review/scripts/finding_votes.py tally, never by hand. `independent` = `validators` fresh Agent validators each voted on every candidate at or above the floor, and only candidates with at least `quorum` confirms at or above `confidence_floor` are in findings. `no-candidates` = no candidate reached the ballot, so no validator was spawned. Counts only: a rejected candidate is recorded nowhere as a finding. That each validator ran in a fresh context is self-reported, like judged_blind. DEV-REVIEW-V1.

validators.description: Validators the ballot was put to (0 when no candidate reached it).

validators_returned.description: Usable ballots returned; a missing or malformed one is never a confirm.

candidates.description: Candidate findings after dedup, below-floor ones included.

split.description: Rejected candidates that at least one validator confirmed.

source.description: The limits file the numbers came from, `<path>#review_validation`.

next_action.description: OPTIONAL hint for the recipe; the router still derives its action from verdict.

attempt.description: OPTIONAL (v1.1.0). Which attempt of this stage produced the artifact, 1-based. Added because the retry audit had to be reconstructed from session transcripts — no artifact recorded its own attempt number, so a retry was indistinguishable from a first pass after the fact. A retry requires transient-failure evidence; a deterministic failure escalates or changes strategy instead of repeating.

retry_reason.description: OPTIONAL (v1.1.0). Why this attempt happened, when attempt > 1 — the flaky-store match, infra error, timeout or oracle exit 2 that justified it.

timing.description: OPTIONAL (v1.1.0). When this stage ran. Costs microseconds to write and is the only way to tell whether a pipeline redesign still holds months later — without it every duration has to be reconstructed from session transcripts, which do not always exist.

judged_blind.description: OPTIONAL (v1.1.0). Did a context that had NOT produced the thing being judged write this artifact? True only when the skill was invoked via Agent with a fresh context. False means the producer graded itself — well-formed, but not an independent verdict.

model.description: OPTIONAL (v1.1.0). The model this ran on. The checker node enforces judge-strength: a judge weaker than the producer it grades yields an invalid verdict, not merely a weaker one.
